issues.description: The solution's toString() method has an incorrect return type: it is declared as 'public Object toString()' (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 63-71). The problem statement explicitly asks for a custom toString() (problem_statement.md lines 36-38) and, per Java's Object API and common expectation, toString() must return a String. Declaring toString() to return Object prevents a valid @Override of Object.toString(), will cause a compilation error, and thus blocks students from running or testing the class as intended.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the toString() method's signature in the solution to 'public String toString()' (and ensure it returns a String). This aligns with the problem statement's requirement and Java's Object.toString() contract, restores a valid @Override, and ensures the class compiles and behaves as expected.
